title: Higher-Dimensional Littlewood Polynomials and Minimum Modulus

problemStatement.formal: For d-variate Littlewood polynomials f(z_1,\ldots,z_d)=\sum_{k\in[n]^d}\varepsilon_k z_1^{k_1}\cdots z_d^{k_d}, with \varepsilon_k\in\{-1,+1\}, study m(f)=\min_{z\in\mathbb{T}^d}|f(z)| and whether random examples satisfy m(f)\le (n^d)^{-1/2+o(1)} for d\ge 2.
problemStatement.plain: This asks how the solved one-variable minimum-modulus theory for random Littlewood polynomials should extend to polynomials in several complex variables on the d-dimensional torus.
whyMatters: It tests whether the one-dimensional square-root scale for random Littlewood polynomials persists after replacing n terms by n^d multivariate terms.
It separates the solved one-dimensional Erdős 525 theory from the open higher-dimensional analogue.

knowledge.markdown:
# Knowledge Base: erdos-525-oq-02

## Problem Understanding

This problem asks for higher-dimensional generalizations of Erdős 525. In one variable, a Littlewood polynomial has coefficients in {-1,+1} and minimum modulus m(f)=min_{|z|=1}|f(z)|. The OQ asks what happens for d-variate Littlewood polynomials on the d-torus.

## Evidence From Parent Erdős 525

The parent proof metadata marks Erdős 525 as solved but axiomatized. The Lean source defines the one-dimensional objects and proves summary wrapper theorems from five axioms: almost_all_small, kashin_theorem, konyagin_upper_bound, cook_nguyen_lambda, and cook_nguyen_distribution. These axioms encode the Kashin, Konyagin, and Cook-Nguyen inputs rather than proving them analytically in Lean.

## Higher-Dimensional OQ State

The OQ Lean development contains setup for multivariate Littlewood polynomials, a torus predicate, and minimum modulus over torus evaluations. Its Lean-proved content is arithmetic/setup level: nontriviality of n^d and 2^(n^d), monotonicity with dimension, and a comparison n^d >= n. The claimed scale n^(-d/2+o(1)) is presented as a square-root cancellation heuristic and remains open for d >= 2 in the local notes.

## Next Steps

Move from OBSERVE to ORIENT by choosing the exact multivariate probability model, stating the d >= 2 conjecture conservatively, and identifying which one-dimensional parent definitions can be reused without importing axiomatized conclusions as if they were new proofs.
